affiliations.occupation: Semiskilled occupation in the manufacture of automobiles, not elsewhere classified
affiliations.date_precision: The official Army-entry record carries civilian occupation code 602 on October 24, 1940; the code names no employer or specific trade.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms the Army-entry row. The occupational group does not establish a company, job title, plant, union, self-employment, or the later Army-to-OSS sequence.

affiliations.role_title: Instructor in German and tutor in Comparative Philology
affiliations.date_precision: Year precision; the institutional memorial explicitly dates both appointments to 1938-41.
affiliations.research_notes: The employment is explicit and precedes Beeler's 1941 Berkeley appointment. It is earlier documented prewar work, not his last civilian employer before wartime service.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: the Berkeley campus of our University
affiliations.date_precision: Year precision; the memorial dates his Berkeley appointment from 1941 and wartime Naval Reserve service from 1942-44. It does not say whether the academic appointment formally ended or continued on leave.
affiliations.research_notes: Berkeley is the last documented civilian employer before the source's 1942-44 Naval Reserve chronology. The evidence does not establish that Berkeley immediately preceded OSS recruitment or that there was no intervening military assignment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Private David Bedor is confirmed as the same person in the official Army-entry file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact private identifier, exact indexed name, and compatible enlisted status establish the record linkage; the identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact private identifier, exact surname and given name, and compatible enlisted Army status.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official record dates Army entry to October 24, 1940; subsequent OSS chronology is not established.
claims.match_notes: The decisive private identifier remains restricted and is never exposed in public data.

claims.claim_text: At Army entry in October 1940, David Bedor's civilian occupation was classified as semiskilled work in automobile manufacture, not elsewhere classified.
claims.evidence_excerpt: 6-02. Occupations in manufacture of automobiles, n.e.c.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact-matched Army row carries code 602; NARA's code list identifies a semiskilled automobile-manufacturing group but names no employer or trade.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private-identifier match confirms that the Army-entry row belongs to the indexed person.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to Army entry on October 24, 1940, but not proven to be his final civilian role before OSS.
claims.match_notes: No automaker, plant, job title, union, self-employment status, or intervening affiliation is inferred.

claims.claim_text: The OSS index's private identifier for Henry W. Beecher Jr. conflicts with the official Army merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The printed private identifier resolves to a differently named Army entrant, while a separate exact-name Army row carries another identifier; neither is reassigned.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Conflicting. The OSS index row is clear, but its private identifier belongs to another name in the separate official Army conversion; the exact-name Army row has a different identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: No Army-entry date, civilian occupation, or sequence from the name-only row is assigned until original records are compared.
claims.match_notes: The unrelated Army identity and both private identifiers are withheld. Box 46 and the original Army cards must be compared.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Madison S. Beeler is a high-confidence match to Berkeley linguist Madison Scott Beeler.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive exact name, full middle name, wartime age, 1942-44 Naval Reserve service, and Lieutenant junior-grade status support the identification.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence. The name is distinctive and the institutional chronology supplies multiple compatible wartime and professional identifiers, but the memorial does not explicitly mention OSS or Box 46.
claims.temporal_assessment: Academic employment is dated 1938-42 and Naval Reserve service 1942-44; the OSS sequence remains unestablished.
claims.match_notes: The match is not promoted to confirmed without a direct OSS personnel-file or service linkage.

claims.claim_text: Madison S. Beeler worked at Harvard University from 1938 through 1941 as an instructor in German and tutor in Comparative Philology.
claims.evidence_excerpt: appointing him, for a period of three years (1938-41), instructor in the University Department of German
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional memorial explicitly names Harvard, both appointments, and their 1938-41 dates.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identification based on the distinctive exact name and compatible wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly documented prewar employment, followed by a 1941 Berkeley appointment; not the last civilian employer before wartime service.
claims.match_notes: His earlier Harvard student status is not treated as employment; only the named 1938-41 appointments are published here.

claims.claim_text: The University of California's Berkeley campus is Madison S. Beeler's best-supported last civilian employer before his 1942-44 Naval Reserve service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: his transfer to the Berkeley campus of our University, where he started at the level of instructor
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The memorial places Beeler at Berkeley from 1941 and then dates his wartime Naval Reserve service to 1942-44.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identification based on the distinctive exact name and compatible wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last documented civilian employer before military service; not established as the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
claims.match_notes: The source does not say whether Beeler formally left Berkeley or took military leave, and it does not establish the timing of OSS recruitment.
